glossary.definition: An event that could have caused harm but did not.
A rating set from the level of harm, actual or potential, defined by the organization.
An action taken to remove the cause of an incident so it does not recur.
The role accountable for decisions and records in a defined workflow.
An event that caused harm, damage, or a stoppage.
A report of a condition noticed before any event occurred.
Statements a demonstration can prove or fail to prove.
The record of the first-review step.
A record of each field’s name, who completes it, whether it is required, and its accepted values.
A set of harm-based rating levels with definitions and examples.
A table naming who is told at each severity level, the expected first-response time, and a fallback role.
A record of the original rating and changes, including who made them, when, and why.
A checklist of applicable external notification duties, responsible roles, and filing records.
A record naming the investigator, investigation scope and date.
A list of evidence items noting what each item is, who collected it, when and where it is held.
A record of the investigation’s explanation that distinguishes observations, reports and conclusions and identifies supporting evidence.
An investigation conclusion recorded with the reviewer’s name and date.
An action that deals with the immediate problem.
The person who makes an action's change or sees that it is made.
A check of whether a completed action worked.
A record of what each group may see.
A proposal for a change.
The point at which the new system becomes the record.
A record listing, for each clause in scope, what the requirement asks, the records held, where they are kept and who owns them.
A list of audit rehearsal gaps with an owner and date for each item.
A log of consequential failures in the reporting process.
An initial set of results used as the starting point for later comparisons.

roles: Joint health and safety committee or health and safety representative
